facts.claim: From 1 January 2026 Paris's taxe de séjour, all shares included, is per person per night: €15.93 at palaces, €11.70 at five-star, €8.45 at four-star, €5.53 at three-star, €3.25 at two-star and €2.60 at one-star hotels, B&Bs and hostels; unclassified lodging pays 5% of the per-person price, capped at €15.93; minors are exempt.

sources.title: City of Paris: tourist tax rates from 1 January 2026 (PDF)
City of Paris: taxe de séjour, exemptions

facts.claim: The Louvre charges €32 to visitors who are neither residents nor citizens of the European Economic Area and €22 to EEA visitors; under-18s are free; it is closed on Tuesdays and opens until 9pm on Wednesdays and Fridays, and recommends booking a time slot.

facts.note: The new non-EEA price was widely reported as starting on 14 January 2026; the official page shows the prices but not the date, so the guide gives no date.

facts.claim: At the start of October 2026 ETIAS was not in operation and no travel-authorisation applications were being collected; the EU says it will announce the start date several months before launch, and the application fee will be €20.

The EU Entry/Exit System registers the entries and exits of non-EU short-stay visitors electronically, with fingerprint and face data, and is gradually replacing passport stamps (Cyprus and Ireland still stamp passports).
